diagnosis: A disruption in the shared optical access path for OLT PON port 0/8/1 is the supported diagnosis. The fault is localized to the common PON service path, but the available evidence does not determine whether the OLT interface, feeder, splitter, or common distribution segment is responsible.
reasoning: The 12 affected buildings share PON port 0/8/1 and splitter S-08, and all 12 ONUs went offline at the same time. The LOS/LOF alarms on that shared PON path are consistent with a common optical-path disruption. The neighboring PON port and its buildings remain in service, which confines the observed impact to the 0/8/1 service path rather than showing a broader access outage. Because no component-level test or physical inspection result is provided, the evidence cannot locate the fault within that shared path.
case_input: Topology: OLT PON port 0/8/1 feeds splitter S-08, which serves 12 building ONUs. Each ONU provides FTTB service to subscribers in its building. At 14:06, all 12 ONUs on this PON port went offline and subscribers in all 12 buildings lost service. The OLT reports LOS and LOF on PON port 0/8/1. The neighboring PON port 0/8/2 remains online, and its served buildings report no service interruption. No individual ONU recovery or building-level restoration has been recorded. The available checks do not identify a physical break location or verify the condition of the OLT PON interface, feeder, splitter, or common distribution segment.
excluded_causes: A single subscriber drop or one building ONU fault cannot explain the simultaneous outage of all 12 ONUs on the same PON port. A broader outage affecting the neighboring PON port is inconsistent with that port and its served buildings remaining online. The evidence does not distinguish an OLT PON interface fault from a feeder, splitter, or common distribution-path fault, so none of those specific components can be ruled in or out.
supporting_evidence: All 12 buildings served by PON port 0/8/1 through splitter S-08 lost service at the same time, and all 12 ONUs went offline. The OLT reports LOS and LOF on 0/8/1. Neighboring PON port 0/8/2 and its served buildings remain online. No inspection or test result identifies the failed component or physical location.
